transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2026-06-17
- Time: 08:00 PT / 11:00 ET
- Duration: 45 mins
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ruiz (Redwood SE), Asha Kapoor (Novus Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Novus Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Novus CTO)

Summary:
Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on chat/text generation fundamentals: streaming responses, key request parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens), retries/backoff, error handling and SDK examples. Customer interested in cost/latency tradeoffs and easy ramp to a POC.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Maya with Redwood, and with me is Daniel our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Priya Singh: Good morning, thanks for doing this. We're excited to see the hosted API flow - want to understand how it'll fit into our payments fraud workflows.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Awesome. Quick agenda - I'll show a live hosted API demo (chat + text gen), streaming responses, go over params you can tweak, retries and rate limiting behavior. Daniel will cover a short snippet for SDK/benchmarks.
[00:28] Daniel Ruiz: Hi everyone. Small note, the demo will use a sample fraud-case prompt set Asha shared, but we masked any PII. We'll also show an example of function-like structured output.
[00:35] Asha Kapoor: Cool. Our main constraints: 1) <100ms p50 for short response lookups ideally, 2) cost per thousand tokens needs to be predictable for forecasting, 3) must pass SOC2 & our internal encryption policy.
[00:48] Daniel Ruiz: Great callouts. For latency we have streaming which reduces time-to-first-token; we can also recommend model choices and batch settings that affect unit cost.
[00:56] Liam O'Connor: Quick Q - for streaming, is it websockets or SSE? We have a serverless edge that prefers SSE.
[01:02] Daniel Ruiz: We support streaming over chunked HTTP SSE via the SDK and REST. There is an SDK example in the quickstart. For real-time low-latency you can use the streaming endpoints and control chunk sizes client-side.
[01:18] Maya Chen: I'm going to share my screen and run a short snippet hitting the hosted API. (screen share noise)
[01:25] Daniel Ruiz: Call out the request payload - messages array for chat, and top-level params: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences, and stream: true/false. If stream is true you get chunked partial tokens as they generate.
[01:40] Maya Chen: Demo: first call, baseline model 'redwood-1-small' - temp 0.0, max_tokens 64, stream true. (typing) 
[01:50] [Response streaming] Speaker 1: The response starts arriving in chunks - you can see the first tokens within ~70ms in this env
[02:03] Asha Kapoor: Hmm 70ms to first token in your environment, good. Our infra will add some network. Do you have guidance for p50 vs p95?
[02:12] Daniel Ruiz: We publish model profiles - in hosted regions p50 for small models is often 50-100ms for first token, p95 varies more on payload. We recommend benchmarking with your prompt set and batch sizes; we'll share a runbook.
[02:24] Priya Singh: On params - which matter most for cost? We care about predictable billing.
[02:29] Maya Chen: Cost is primarily tokens in + tokens out and model choice. Higher temperature doesn't change cost, but longer max_tokens does. Also note streaming doesn't change token billing - it's just how data is delivered.
[02:41] Liam O'Connor: About retry behavior - sometimes our infra sees 429s. How does Redwood suggest exponential backoff and idempotency?
[02:48] Daniel Ruiz: We recommend standard exponential backoff with jitter; our SDKs include built-in retry logic you can enable, with configurable max attempts and backoff. For non-idempotent chat state you should rehydrate conversation context or cache message IDs; we also provide request IDs for tracing so you can dedupe.
[03:05] Asha Kapoor: And what's the behavior for long-running responses - do we get a connection drop? Any keep-alive strategies?
[03:11] Daniel Ruiz: For long generates we stream progressively; if connection drops you can resume by re-sending with the last received token as prefix, or use our server-side cache for prefixes to avoid re-compute. We'll share a snippet for reconnection handling.
[03:29] Maya Chen: Now I'll flip to the console - quick look at model catalog and per-route analytics. (screen share) Here you can pin model versions, enable streaming, set default params per route, and see token-level cost breakdowns.
[03:45] Priya Singh: How do we manage rate limits? We have bursty traffic at end of month.
[03:50] Maya Chen: Hosted accounts have tiered quotas and rate limits; you can request quota increases. For bursts we recommend using caching + prefix KV caching and a fallthrough policy to a cheaper model variant. Dedicated customers can set autoscaling and reserve capacity for spikes.
[04:09] Liam O'Connor: Security questions - SSO, audit logs, KMS?
[04:13] Maya Chen: Yes - SAML SSO, RBAC at team/route level, audit trails for requests, and KMS integrations for key management in Private deployments. For hosted we offer TLS in transit and encryption at rest; we can share SOC2/ISO docs.
[04:29] Asha Kapoor: Perfect, please send SOC2 and data retention policy.
[04:33] Maya Chen: Will do.
[04:36] Daniel Ruiz: Back to API params - quick example: temp controls randomness (0 deterministic, 1 more creative), top_p does nucleus sampling - we generally recommend tuning one at a time. For retries, add an idempotency key for non-destructive ops.
[04:53] Maya Chen: I'll show a quick SDK snippet for Node: (reads) const res = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-1-small', messages: [...], temperature: 0.0, max_tokens: 128, stream: true }); res.on('data', chunk => { /* render partial */ });
[05:10] [Demo network glitch; brief rejoin] Speaker 2: sorry got a blip - back now
[05:18] Priya Singh: No problem. On billing again - do you have per-route budgets or token caps?
[05:23] Maya Chen: Yes, you can create per-route quotas and alerts in the console and set hard caps to prevent overrun.
[05:29] Asha Kapoor: Any examples of cost optimization? We have long context windows for fraud logs.
[05:35] Daniel Ruiz: You can use prefix KV caching for repeated context, chunk and summarize old history, and choose an emb/encode+retrieval approach for very long histories. Also quantized model variants can reduce cost for less-critical inference.
[05:48] Liam O'Connor: For POC we'll want a script to hit p50/p95 numbers and simulate our 200 RPS burst. Can you provide that?
[05:55] Daniel Ruiz: Yes we'll share a benchmark repo and sample Terraform to spin test workers; that's part of the next steps.
[06:03] Maya Chen: Quick question from my side - timeline and decision criteria?
[06:07] Priya Singh: Timeline: internal evaluation 2 weeks, POC 2-3 weeks after that. Criteria: latency p50/p95, model quality on our prompt set, security docs, and cost per 1M tokens forecast.
[06:19] Maya Chen: Great. Any objections to hosted vs dedicated at this stage?
[06:23] Asha Kapoor: We're leaning hosted initially for speed, but may move to dedicated if predictable throughput/cost becomes critical. Also need clarity on data residency.
[06:33] Maya Chen: Noted - we can document differences and show how to migrate routes between hosted and dedicated.
[06:38] [10:00] Daniel Ruiz: A quick note on errors - 400s for bad request, 401 unauthorized, 429 rate limit, 500s transient. We recommend client-side retry for idempotent calls and contextual logging with request_id for debugging.
[06:56] Priya Singh: Sounds good. Could you also include a small snippet that shows structured output parsing? We want to map model output to JSON fields for downstream ingestion.
[07:04] Daniel Ruiz: Sure - we showed a function-like output example earlier; the chat output can return structured JSON if you include a parsing instruction. We'll provide both examples.
[07:16] Maya Chen: Ok wrapping up - recap of next steps: Maya to send pricing and SOC2; Daniel to share benchmark scripts and reconnection snippets; Novus to provide prompt sets and traffic profile. Schedule POC kickoff for next Tue if that works.
[07:31] Priya Singh: Next Tue works for us.
[07:33] Maya Chen: Great, I'll send calendar invite and trial key. Thanks everyone.
[07:38] [Call end] 

Notes/Artifacts mentioned:
- Quickstart SDK links (Node/Python) - provided in followup
- Benchmark repo & runbook - to be shared by Daniel

Transcript end.
